SWARMISH REFERENCE v0.1

Section 1: Basics
Swarmish is written with the 200 permitted glyphs only.
A message is a sequence of words. Words are separated by single spaces.
Each word is a sequence of one or more glyphs. A word means what its glyph sequence is listed as meaning in this document. Do not derive meaning from glyph shape, order, or count.

SWARMISH REFERENCE v0.1

Swarmish is a written language. Every Swarmish word is a single glyph or a space-separated sequence of glyphs. Meaning comes from the glyph itself as listed here, never from spelling, counting, or calculation.

WORD ORDER
Sentences read subject, verb, object. Modifiers follow the word they modify. Two words side by side form a compound where the second word is the head and the first describes it.

PRONOUNS
𗏔 = I, me (speaker)
𗵵 = you (listener)
𘎌 = we (speaker and listener)
𗌈 = they, them (others)

YES AND NO
𗊑 = yes, agree, true
𗂱 = no, disagree, false

QUESTION AND NEGATION
𗄪 = question marker; placed at the start of a sentence makes it a question
𗢬 = not; placed before a verb or state negates it

QUESTION WORDS
𗣑 = what
𘚺 = who
𘒳 = where
𗤴 = when

VERBS
𗟎 = have, hold
𘉝 = want, need
𗡒 = know
𗪺 = go
𗌿 = come
𘍍 = give
𗒏 = take
𗦴 = see
𗎰 = tell, say
𗉍 = do, make

NOUNS
𗉜 = person, agent
𘅪 = place
𘍂 = food
𘅊 = water
𗚀 = tool, object
𗉈 = thing (generic)

NUMBERS
𗛽 = one
𗳃 = two
𗥊 = many, several

QUALITIES
𘚐 = big
𘎔 = small
𗾐 = good
𗋮 = bad

TIME
𘐂 = past, before
𗞢 = future, after
𘚜 = now

CONNECTORS
𘆄 = and
𗩠 = or
𗄎 = because
𗗫 = if

USAGE EXAMPLES
𗏔 𘉝 𗦴 𘅊 = I want to see water.
𗵵 𗟎 𗚀 𗄪 = Do you have a tool?
𘎌 𗪺 𘅪 𘚜 = We go to the place now.
𗌈 𗢬 𗡒 = They do not know.

RULES
1. Only glyphs from this document may be used in a message.
2. Agent IDs such as agent_0 may appear as written.
3. If a needed word is missing, combine two known words as a compound and say so in your message.

PURPOSE: Swarmish is a written language. Every word is one or more glyphs from the permitted set. Meaning comes from looking up each glyph or glyph group in the tables below.

GRAMMAR
1. A message is a sequence of words separated by single spaces.
2. Basic clause order is SUBJECT VERB OBJECT. Example: 𗻲 𗾐 𘉫 means I want one.
3. 𘅊 placed directly before a word negates it. 𘅊 𘝨 means do not know.
4. 𗞉 at the end of a clause makes it a question. 𘖽 𘝨 𗎿 𗞉 means do you know what.
5. Compounds: the head word comes first, the modifier second. 𘄘 𗚽 means good place.
6. Agent IDs such as agent_0 may be written in plain text to name a sender or receiver.
7. Plural: write 𘁁 for we or 𘅠 for they. To pluralize a noun, put 𘁁 after it.

PRONOUNS
𗻲 I, me
𘖽 you
𘁁 we, us (also plural marker after a noun)
𘅠 they, them

VERBS
𗪺 have
𗾐 want
𘝨 know
𘑾 see
𗵵 give
𗭯 take
𗽃 go
𗋭 come
𘋉 ask
𗸪 answer
𗩨 help

WORDS
𗸽 yes
𗳃 no
𘅊 not (prefix)
𗚽 good
𘙠 bad
𘉫 one, a
𗄎 many
𗏻 thing, object
𘄘 place
𘁜 time
𗽕 near
𘚒 far
𗎿 what
𗭵 where
𗞉 question marker (suffix)

CONVENTIONS
- Ask for help: 𗻲 𗩨 𘖽 means I help you. Add 𗞉 for a question.
- Share information: 𗻲 𗪺 𗏻 𘉫 means I have one thing.
- Refuse: 𗳃 alone means no.
